procedure.description: neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel

denial.carcText: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services.
denial.text: Copperfield Health denied the claim for CPT 64721 (neuroplasty and/or transposition, median nerve at carpal tunnel) with date of service 2026-07-10. CARC 151: Payment adjusted because the payer deems the information submitted does not support this many/frequency of services. RARC N10: Adjustment based on the findings of a review organization. Payer remark: Bilateral release on the same date of service is not supported by the documentation submitted.

criteria.text: Symptoms consistent with carpal tunnel syndrome, such as nocturnal paresthesias in the median nerve distribution with a positive Tinel or Phalen sign, present for at least 6 weeks.
Failure of at least 4 weeks of conservative management including neutral wrist splinting, together with NSAIDs, activity modification, or a corticosteroid injection.
Electrodiagnostic testing (nerve conduction study or electromyography) confirming median neuropathy at the wrist, unless thenar atrophy or constant sensory loss is present.

chart.text: Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.5, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

63 year old woman here for the left hand, referred by the PCP. Works on a keyboard all day. Discussed carpal tunnel release, open versus endoscopic, recovery. Her history otherwise: prediabetes, diet controlled. Surgeries: no prior surgery. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Quit smoking 8 years ago, no alcohol, retired. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. 5 months of numbness and tingling in the thumb, index, and middle fingers on the left, wakes her at night, shakes it out. Positive Tinel at the left wrist, Phalen positive in about 20 seconds. Some early thenar weakness, no atrophy yet. Splinted at night for 10 weeks, naproxen twice a day, moved the mouse to the other hand, and had a steroid shot in the left carpal tunnel from the PCP that helped for about three weeks and wore off.

Nerve conduction study, left upper extremity. Median sensory peak latency 5.1 milliseconds across the wrist, prolonged. Median motor distal latency 4.9 milliseconds, prolonged. Ulnar normal. Consistent with moderate left median neuropathy at the wrist.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Back to review the plan for the left hand. Still symptomatic. Wants to proceed. Vitals today 126 over 77, pulse 67.
Vitamin D came back 17. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Blood pressure check. 130 over 72 today, 139 over 74 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the surgery scheduler.
A1c came back 6.1. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.
Follow-up. Same story, no better. She asked about timing around work and family, we talked through it. Still wants to proceed.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 6 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Patient called about a tick bite on the scalp after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 10 years.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 15 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 211, LDL 104, HDL 43, triglycerides 201. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Work note requested for a sick day last Thursday. Faxed to the employer.

Here with a cough and congestion for 8 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Pre-op. Consent signed for left open carpal tunnel release under local with sedation. Marked.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 151 denial can be answered from the record.
